All these applications are filed seeking anticipatory bail.

2. Petitioner is the accused No.1 in Crime Nos.862/2023 in B.A. No.6101/2024 and in all the other bail applications, he is the 2nd accused in crime Nos.785/2023, 783/2023, 774/2023, 841/2023,
782/2023, 781/2023, of Shakthikulangara Police Station, Kollam.
The offences alleged against the petitioners are punishable under Sections 420 and 34 of IPC.

3. The prosecution case is that A1 and A2 are the Managing Directors, A3 is the manager and A4 is the consultant of Japan Nursing Care Farm Jobs 'GDGH Private Limited' near Vallikkeezhu Junction in Sakthikulangara Bail Appl. Nos.6101/2024, 6098/2024, 6107/2024, 6134/2024,
6137/2024, 2024:KER:74930 village.

entities.text: Japan Nursing Care Farm Jobs 'GDGH Private Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Through social media apps, the accused advertised overseas employment in Japan stating that an employment visa as Health Care Taker in Japan would be provided on payment of Rs.3,60,000/-.

Believing the said advertisement, when the defacto complainant approached the said institution, the accused dishonestly induced him to deliver Rs.10,000/- towards the registration fee and subsequently Rs.1,25,000/- on various occasions.
As per the prosecution case, the accused also induced one Jerry Peter, Amal Joseph, and Mibin and collected Rs.5,45,000/-.

Many job seekers have fallen prey to the fraud committed by the accused and the accused have misappropriated several lakhs of rupees by duping the job seekers and thereby committed the offences mentioned above.
4. When the applications for anticipatory bail were filed, the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that his client was abroad and intended to come to India on 15.09.2024.

He had also produced a copy of the travel tickets Bail Appl. Nos.6101/2024, 6098/2024, 6107/2024, 6134/2024,
6137/2024, 2024:KER:74930 showing the above.

Accordingly, this Court passed an order on 11.09.2024 as follows:-
"The learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that his client who is abroad, intends to travel to India on 15.09.2024 and has produced a copy of the travel ticket showing the above.
It is ordered that the petitioner shall not be arrested on his arrival in India.
However, the petitioner shall surrender his passport before the Investigating Officer within three days of his arrival.
It will also be open to the Investigating Officer to interrogate the petitioner for four days between 10.00 am and 5.00 pm.
The Investigating Officer shall thereafter file a report before this Court so as to enable this Court to consider the application for anticipatory bail.
The petitioner shall not be arrested till 03.10.2024 if he complies with the directions in this order.

"
Augustine Xavier vs State Of Kerala on 9 October, 2024

Pursuant to the above order the petitioner had appeared before the Investigating Officer and surrendered his passport bearing No.Z4465089 on 18.09.2024.
He had also appeared before the Investigating Officer as directed by this Court.

6. Taking note of the above and that the petitioner complied with the order passed by this Court and is Bail Appl. Nos.6101/2024, 6098/2024, 6107/2024, 6134/2024, 6137/2024, 2024:KER:74930 cooperating with the investigation, I do not think that the custodial interrogation of the petitioner is required.

I also notice that the 2nd accused was granted regular bail by this Court by orders dated 27th September 2023 in Bail Appl. No.8005 of 2023 and connected cases, wherein it was found that all the documents/bank documents were already seized by the police.
5. He shall not leave the State of Kerala without the permission of the Court having jurisdiction;
6. He shall not leave India without the permission of the jurisdictional Court.
7. If any of the conditions are violated, the court concerned will be empowered to take steps for cancellation of bail as per law.

opennyai_summary.facts:
All these applications are filed seeking anticipatory bail.
The offences alleged against the petitioners are punishable under Sections 420 and 34 of IPC.
Through social media apps, the accused advertised overseas employment in Japan stating that an employment visa as Health Care Taker in Japan would be provided on payment of Rs.3,60,000/-.
Believing the said advertisement, when the defacto complainant approached the said institution, the accused dishonestly induced him to deliver Rs.10,000/- towards the registration fee and subsequently Rs.1,25,000/- on various occasions.
As per the prosecution case, the accused also induced one Jerry Peter, Amal Joseph, and Mibin and collected Rs.5,45,000/-.
Many job seekers have fallen prey to the fraud committed by the accused and the accused have misappropriated several lakhs of rupees by duping the job seekers and thereby committed the offences mentioned above.
4. When the applications for anticipatory bail were filed, the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that his client was abroad and intended to come to India on 15.09.2024.
Accordingly, this Court passed an order on 11.09.2024 as follows:-
"The learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that his client who is abroad, intends to travel to India on 15.09.2024 and has produced a copy of the travel ticket showing the above.
He had also appeared before the Investigating Officer as directed by this Court.
opennyai_summary.decision:
It is ordered that the petitioner shall not be arrested on his arrival in India.
However, the petitioner shall surrender his passport before the Investigating Officer within three days of his arrival.
It will also be open to the Investigating Officer to interrogate the petitioner for four days between 10.00 am and 5.00 pm.
The Investigating Officer shall thereafter file a report before this Court so as to enable this Court to consider the application for anticipatory bail.
The petitioner shall not be arrested till 03.10.2024 if he complies with the directions in this order.
I also notice that the 2nd accused was granted regular bail by this Court by orders dated 27th September 2023 in Bail Appl. No.8005 of 2023 and connected cases, wherein it was found that all the documents/bank documents were already seized by the police.
Under the said circumstances,
I am inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner on the following grounds:-
1. The petitioner shall be released on bail on executing a bond for Rs.200,000/-
(Rupees Two lakhs only) each with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional court;
2. He shall report before the Investigating Officer as and when directed;
3. He shall not tamper or attempt to tamper with the evidence or influence or try to influence the witnesses;
4. He shall not be involved in any other crime while Bail Appl. Nos.6101/2024,
6098/2024, 6107/2024, 6134/2024, 6137/2024, 2024:KER:74930 on bail.
5. He shall not leave the State of Kerala without the permission of the Court having jurisdiction;
6. He shall not leave India without the permission of the jurisdictional Court.
7. If any of the conditions are violated, the court concerned will be empowered to take steps for cancellation of bail as per law.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS: 6. Taking note of the above and that the petitioner complied with the order passed by this Court and is Bail Appl. Nos.6101/2024, 6098/2024, 6107/2024, 6134/2024, 6137/2024, 2024:KER:74930 cooperating with the investigation, I do not think that the custodial interrogation of the petitioner is required.
